writeup.headline: Tempus AI rates Hold: fast growth and strong momentum offset by losses, cash burn and weak valuation support
writeup.thesis: Tempus AI scores 47, a Hold, just 3 points above the Sell line. The strongest supports are the trend score of 73, with the price 34.7% above its 200-day average and shares 44.1 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and a balance sheet score of 73 backed by cash at 3.19 times debt. Growth scores 65 on TTM revenue growth of 50.4%, but growth slowed by 14.6 pp from the previous quarter, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 21.6% year on year. Quality is the weakest factor at 11: the operating margin is -19.8%, the FCF margin is -18.4%, stock-based pay runs at 13.0% of revenue, and the diluted share count is up 5.2% year on year. Valuation scores 17 because negative FCF and EBIT leave no P/FCF or EV/EBIT, and there is no comparison with its own history; news is mildly positive at 66 on analyst target raises and new pharma deals.
key_risks: Continued losses and cash burn, with about 2.3 years of cash at the current burn rate
Revenue growth is decelerating, slowed by 14.6 pp from the previous quarter
Ongoing dilution, with the diluted share count up 5.2% year on year and stock-based pay at 13.0% of revenue
Q3 results due around Nov 2 and integration of the Personalis acquisition could disappoint
Momentum-driven share price, still 14.7% below its 52-week high, could reverse quickly
what_would_change: A drop of just 3 points, for example from weaker trend or news after Q3 results, would move the rating to Sell
Narrowing operating and FCF losses toward the roughly $65M Adjusted EBITDA guidance would lift the quality score of 11
Re-accelerating revenue growth would help the growth score, though reaching Buy needs 18 more points
Turning FCF positive would allow valuation multiples to be measured and could raise the valuation score of 17
